summary: Background telemetry pings counted against tenant quota causing intermittent 429s during bulk ingest
description: Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses during a large daily ingest job despite reported quota remaining available. Impact: Multiple hourly bulk uploads fail with client-visible 429s; ingestion lag increased by ~3x and customer throttled their downstream pipelines. Environment: Dedicated pool (Cerebro Analytics), prod us-east-1, persistent API keys, mixed streaming and REST uploads. Steps to reproduce: follow their scheduled bulk ingest (described below) while telemetry_agent enabled. Observed behavior: Throttles spike coincident with background telemetry/heartbeat pings from the customer's ingestion workers. Each heartbeat appears to be accounted against the tenant token bucket, causing cumulative depletion during high-frequency fanout. Expected behavior: Internal telemetry pings (health/heartbeat) should not consume user quota or should be classified under a non-billed/low-priority channel. Logs & evidence: request_ids and dashboard captures attached (see logs_and_evidence). Additional notes: Customer rotated keys yesterday as part of their CI; however throttles persisted before and after rotation. The issue started after customer enabled the verbose telemetry flag in their ingestion library last week.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs scheduled bulk ingest across 40 parallel workers against /v1/streams and /v1/embeddings endpoints
2) Each worker also sends telemetry heartbeat every 30s to /internal/heartbeat (newer SDK flag enabled)
3) Observe tenant token bucket depletion on admin quota dashboard while total billed tokens remain below purchased commit
4) Confirm client receives 429s for subsequent ingest calls until bucket refills
5) Disable telemetry flag and rerun job to verify throttles stop occurring
logs_and_evidence: Sample failed request: req_20260310_ae412 (429) - see linked trace in APM
investigation_notes: Initial triage: Support reproduced tenant bucket drain in staging by enabling telemetry heartbeat at 30s; telemetry pings were routed through the same per-tenant rate-limiter path as public requests.
Hypothesis: telemetry endpoint is not excluded from quota accounting when sent by SDK with customer API key; rate-limiter treats /internal/* calls as regular requests under the tenant token bucket.

Observed in logs: heartbeat requests carry Authorization header with same API key and produce token accounting entries (token_cost ~2 per ping). At 40 workers x 2 pings/min that’s ~160 token/min which contributed to exhaustion during peak ingest.

Related PRs: telemetry-agent PR to mark internal pings as non-billed is open (see related_github_prs). Rate-limiter change may be required to ignore or reclassify specific internal routes for quota accounting.
Customer reported they previously did not see this because telemetry flag was off; change in their SDK default exposed the issue.
comments: Support - Maya Rodriguez - 2026-03-10: Acknowledged receipt, escalated to rate-limiter and infra teams. Collected customer logs and requested time window and sample request IDs.

Customer - Alex Chen (Cerebro) - 2026-03-10: Confirmed pattern; we rolled back telemetry flag mid-job and observed throttles cease within 2 minutes. Happy to provide SSH access to a sample worker for repro.

Infra - James Li - 2026-03-11: Reproduced in staging. Telemetry endpoint currently counts against tenant bucket. Opened PR to tag /internal/heartbeat as exempt; awaiting review from security to ensure no abuse vector.

SRE - Priya Kumar - 2026-03-11: Noted that dedicated pool billing flow still records tokens for internal endpoints; need to coordinate with billing to avoid invoice discrepancies when we exempt these pings.

Support - Maya Rodriguez - 2026-03-12: Shared temporary mitigation steps with customer (disable verbose telemetry or throttle heartbeat frequency). Customer applied mitigation and reported immediate improvement. Working with Eng to track permanent fix.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: instructed customer to disable SDK verbose telemetry or set heartbeat interval to 5m. Engineering path: add route-level exemption in rate-limiter to prevent internal telemetry endpoints from consuming tenant quota and update billing reconciliation to exclude those tokens. Related PRs opened; security review pending. Will monitor post-deploy for 48h before closing.
next_steps: 1) Security review of PR that exempts /internal/heartbeat from quota accounting (assignee: James Li)
2) Billing reconciliation check to ensure no retroactive invoice changes (owner: Finance Eng)
3) Deploy change to staging and run customer test job with telemetry enabled to validate fix (owner: SRE)
4) Post-deploy monitor 48h and confirm zero unexpected 429s; update customer and close ticket
